grh_fe2aa4c0d40c3df104c5.title: The Ransom
paragraphs: Honest plumber Toby McVay idly sketches a supposedly foolproof kidnapping plan after working at the estate of wealthy Mrs. DePaultry, only to let his small-time hustler friend talk him into carrying it out. They abduct her and demand millions, then discover that her fortune is tied up in assets that cannot be converted to cash without attracting police attention. Toby improvises again, releasing her on her word that she will conceal their identities and later pay $100,000. She keeps the first half of the bargain but returns to announce that a promise made under duress does not require her to hand over cash. Instead, she has bought a $100,000 life-insurance policy naming the kidnappers as beneficiaries. If they want the money, they will have to murder the woman they just freed, turning their perfect crime into one final absurd dilemma.

Other credited names include Fletcher Markle as director, Fletcher Markle as producer, Percy Grainger as writer, and [[person|vincent-price|Vincent Price]] as host.
The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.9b0a0ccffce2f7d3|Sears, Roebuck and Company]].

grh_fed74f80f5810fc2603e.title: This Thing Called Love
paragraphs: Business statistician Anne Collins returns from a whirlwind marriage in Rio convinced that romance should be managed scientifically. When her mining-engineer husband Tice comes home after three months away, Anne announces that they will test her new marriage theory with a four-month platonic trial, separate rooms and an intellectual rather than emotional relationship. Tice is appalled but plays along, while Anneâ€™s carefully organized experiment produces jealousy, misunderstandings and escalating schemes. Needing financing from family-minded Peruvian investor SeÃ±or de Estro, Tice falsely implies that Anne is expecting a baby, forcing both spouses deeper into comic deception. Their arguments make it increasingly obvious that neither statistics nor rules can contain their attraction. grh_fe77b614f340daaa8d83.title: The Paleface
paragraphs: The governor sends Calamity Jane undercover to stop renegade Preston from smuggling rifles and dynamite to hostile Indians. To maintain her cover she joins a wagon train and marries timid dentist Painless Peter Potter, who believes he has suddenly become a legendary frontier gunfighter whenever Jane secretly shoots from behind him. Painless basks in his accidental reputation while Preston mistakes him for the government agent and targets him for death. Captured by the Indians, Painless finally learns that his new wife is really Calamity Jane and that all of his miraculous marksmanship was hers. The pair escape in Prestonâ€™s wagon, accidentally setting off the dynamite shipment and destroying the contraband before it reaches the Indians. With the mission complete, Jane admits she loves Painless, although another assignment immediately threatens their long-delayed honeymoon.

grh_fed2af9583f17f5919fc.title: The Hamster Caper of Curtis Cleever
paragraphs: Curtis Cleever and Louise want to marry but Curtis refuses to do it until he has achieved financial independence. His answer is Love for Sale Enterprises, a hamster-breeding business built on the animals' rapid reproduction. The venture quickly outruns his calculations: the hamsters multiply through the apartment, hibernate when the heat fails, chew or escape from delivery boxes, and leave customers chasing animals that were supposed to arrive neatly packaged. With his get-rich plan collapsing into comic chaos, Curtis finally realizes that waiting for perfect financial security has become its own trap. He proposes that he and Louise stop postponing their lives and make the following week their own Independence Day by getting married.
